interest: This document illustrates the U.S. State Department's systematic tracking of Japan's state monopolies and fiscal revenue in the period immediately preceding the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War in 1937. Government monopolies, especially over tobacco, salt, and camphor, served as vital sources of non-tax revenue for the Japanese state budget and burgeoning military programs. Even in docket summary form, it demonstrates the economic intelligence gathered by the American diplomatic post in Tokyo regarding Japanese domestic commerce and fiscal administration.
overview: This file contains the U.S. Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.61331, cataloguing records relating to tobacco in Japan under the broader subject classification of agriculture and alkaloidal plants. The sheet lists a single communication, despatch No. 180 dated February 10, 1937, sent from Tokyo by Consul General Arthur Garrels to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE), reporting an increase in revenues from the Japanese government's tobacco monopoly.

subfiles.summary: This document is a State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet indexing decimal file 894.61331 on tobacco in Japan. It records a single incoming paper, despatch No. 180 sent from Tokyo by Consul General Arthur Garrels on February 10, 1937, and routed to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE). The listed purport indicates that Japanese tobacco monopoly revenues had increased.
